To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“the mitigation of the global warming impact from fresh fruit production can be achieved by adopting climate smart management practices and by recycling the tree biomass at end of life”.

the global warming potential of fresh fruit production in the Mediterranean region can be mitigated by the adoption of sustainable management practices, and this is due to the increase of soil organic carbon stocks.

sustainable management practices can mitigate the global warming potential of fruit orchards in Southern Europe, but the mitigation potential is limited and depends on the site-specific conditions and the management practices implemented.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mitigation of global warming impact from the fresh fruit production through the adoption of climate smart management practices.
the assessment of the global warming impact and the mitigation potential related to the adoption of sustainable management practices in perennial fruit orchards.

the development of a methodology for a comprehensive assessment of the GWP of fruit orchards and of the mitigation potential of sustainable practices in order to support the design and implementation of mitigation strategies at landscape scale.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the adoption of S m ng practices can reduce the global warming impact, but it is necessary to take into account the whole life cycle and all the possible GHGs mitigation options.
the mitigation potential of S mng in fruit orchards is not significant if assessed at farm scale, but could become relevant when assessed at landscape scale.
, although S mng practices have a low impact on GWP, the adoption of S m ng is a good strategy to improve soil quality and related ecosystem services, and to reduce the use of synthetic inputs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the adoption of S m ng practices can contribute to the mitigation of the GWP impact of perennial crops, especially if the carbon stored in soil can be considered.
the mitigation potential of adopting sustainable management practices is higher than the mitigation potential of using composting as a management strategy for the disposal of tree biomass.
the mitigation potential of S mng is mainly related to SOC sequestration, which is the result of a complex interaction of different management practices.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the introduction of sustainable management practices can contribute to the mitigation of global warming potential in the fresh fruit production, especially when accounting for SOC dynamics and for the end-of-life scenario of the orchard.

, when assessing the GHGs mitigation impact of sustainable agricultural management, it is crucial to consider the whole production chain, and the long-term effects of management practices on soil quality and carbon storage.
the adoption of sustainable management practices can be an important tool for reducing the global warming impact associated to the fresh fruit production.
